Answer: D
Reason: The initial chest X-ray shows diffuse, patchy alveolar infiltrates that completely resolve in the follow-up images (Figures 4a and 4b), a pattern characteristic of the rapid clearance of blood seen in recovery from exercise-induced pulmonary haemorrhage (EIPH). Other options like bacterial pneumonia or ARDS typically leave residual changes or resolve more slowly, while cardiogenic edema would likely show cardiac enlargement which is not prominent here.
